name: Mist Trail to Vernal and Nevada Falls
summary: Granite stairs beside two of Yosemite's great waterfalls — soaked in spring spray, with a gentler way down on the John Muir Trail.

details.route: Happy Isles to the top of Nevada Fall via the Mist Trail
details.gettingThere: Free Valley shuttle to Happy Isles (stop #16).
tips: Turn around at the Vernal Fall footbridge (1.6 mi round trip) for a short version.
The lower Mist Trail closes in winter; the John Muir Trail is the alternate route.

sources.label: NPS — Vernal Fall and Nevada Fall Trails

name: Upper Yosemite Fall
summary: One of the park's oldest and toughest trails, climbing beside North America's tallest waterfall to the Valley rim.

details.route: Camp 4 to the top of Yosemite Falls
tips: No water on the trail — the park suggests about 4 quarts for the full hike.
Columbia Rock (2 mi round trip) makes a good shorter goal.

name: Half Dome
summary: The bucket-list day hike: waterfalls, forest, and a final climb up steel cables on bare granite. Permit required.

details.route: Happy Isles to the summit of Half Dome
details.permit: Permit required while the cables are up: preseason lottery on Recreation.gov (apply March 1–31) plus a daily lottery two days before.
details.gettingThere: Free Valley shuttle to Happy Isles (stop #16); start before dawn.
tips: Never go up the cables when the rock is wet or storms are building.
Bring gloves with good grip for the cables.

name: Four Mile Trail to Glacier Point
summary: A relentless switchback climb from the Valley floor to Glacier Point, with Yosemite Falls and Half Dome in view the whole way.

details.route: Valley floor (Southside Drive) to Glacier Point
details.gettingThere: Trailhead on Southside Drive near Sentinel Beach; or hike down from Glacier Point when the road is open.
tips: The trail closes in winter and early spring because of snow and ice.
Combine with the Panorama Trail for a big loop past Nevada and Vernal Falls.

name: Sentinel Dome
summary: A short walk and a scramble up open granite to a 360-degree view of Half Dome, El Capitan and Yosemite Falls.

details.route: Sentinel Dome/Taft Point Trailhead to the summit
details.gettingThere: Glacier Point Road (usually open May–November, depending on conditions).
tips: Stay off the dome during thunderstorms.
Add Taft Point from the same trailhead for cliff-edge views.

name: Annapurna Circuit
summary: The classic loop around the Annapurna massif, from subtropical valleys over the 5,416 m Thorong La to the Kali Gandaki gorge.

details.route: Besisahar to Jomsom over Thorong La
details.permit: ACAP permit; foreign trekkers must hike with a licensed guide.
details.gettingThere: Bus from Kathmandu or Pokhara to Besisahar.
tips: Plan acclimatisation days in Manang before Thorong La.
Roads now cover parts of the route — side trails like the Tilicho Lake detour keep it wild.

name: Annapurna Base Camp
summary: Into the Annapurna Sanctuary: rhododendron forest, Gurung villages and a ring of 7,000 m peaks around base camp.

details.route: Into the Annapurna Sanctuary to Annapurna Base Camp
details.permit: ACAP permit; foreign trekkers must hike with a licensed guide.
details.gettingThere: Drive from Pokhara to the trailhead (Nayapul or further by jeep).
tips: The section above Deurali crosses avalanche terrain — follow local advice after snowfall.
Combine with Poon Hill at the start for a sunrise over Dhaulagiri.

name: Mardi Himal
summary: A quieter ridge trek straight toward Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), with big mountain views from the first days.

details.route: Kande or Phedi to Mardi Himal High Camp and viewpoint
details.permit: ACAP permit; foreign trekkers must hike with a licensed guide.
details.gettingThere: About 1 hour by road from Pokhara to Kande.
tips: Teahouses are smaller here — book ahead in peak season.
Start the viewpoint hike before dawn for clear morning views.
